Blazehowl was the only Flameruff in the Emberpup family to leave behind the legend of "one hundred victories."
He was a lone wolf, without a family or companions, with only a pair of claws that never stayed sheathed and a heart always craving battle.
One hundred victories. One hundred in a row.
That record made Blazehowl an idol to many Emberpups, who told stories of every battle, mimicked every move, and dreamed of one day becoming as strong as him.
But Blazehowl was not happy.
"Winning is too easy," he once told an admiring Emberpup. "I do not want victory. I want the fight itself."
The Emberpup did not understand, only gazing at him with even greater admiration.
Then Icho appeared.
On that day, Blazehowl tasted defeat for the first time. Icho felled him with a single claw.
Blazehowl rose and charged again. Fell. Rose again. Fell again.
In that battle, he lost seven times.
"Impossible," he said, lying on the ground of Thousand-Fang Ridge, staring at the withered Ridgeback Trees. "I should be invincible. I should be the Undefeated Warrior..."
He obsessively challenged Icho. Once, twice, three times... and each challenge ended in defeat. His famed speed meant nothing against Icho, and his crushing strength felt as weak as a breeze.
By the tenth defeat, Blazehowl began to doubt himself.
By the fiftieth defeat, Blazehowl began to fear battle.
By the ninety-ninth defeat, Blazehowl had lost his fighting spirit completely.
On the day of his hundredth defeat, Blazehowl stood at the center of Thousand-Fang Ridge and howled to the sky. It was not a battle cry. It was a wail.
"I lost. I lost completely," he told himself. "I am not the Undefeated Warrior. I am the Hundred-Loss Warrior."
At that moment, a chain appeared around his feet. It was called "fear of failure" and "the inability to accept his imperfect self."
Blazehowl became an Inferlupa.
He no longer challenged anyone, nor did he accept anyone’s challenge. He simply stood in a corner of Thousand-Fang Ridge, silent as a withered tree, cold as stone.
"The Undefeated Warrior is dead," he told every wolf who asked his name. "Now there is only the Hundred-Loss Warrior."
Yet in his heart, a voice still echoed. It was what the admiring Emberpup had said long ago:
"I really, really cannot wait to hear your next victory story!"
Blazehowl closed his eyes. The next victory story... would there ever be one?

In his final moments, Ron looked at the "Beautiful Voice Perfume" and many memories returned to him.
A boy who felt ashamed of his singing met Tucker hiding in a corner, humming an equally off-key tune—and they both stopped feeling sad.
In fact, they began to feel glad, knowing there was "someone else just like me" in the world.
They started singing those awful songs together, louder and louder, more and more joyfully.
And as they sang, their hearts connected, and they gained the power to twine.
"From the moment we twined, we became each other’s greatest friend."
"No matter what happens, that will never change."
————
Ron told this story over and over to his son, again and again, along with the regret of a promise left unfulfilled.
In the end, he set down the perfume and picked up the long-dried glimmer fruit garland.
There was still so much he wanted to say, but by then, he no longer had the strength.
His son held his hand and repeated to him:
"I’ll wear the garland. I’ll find Tucker. I’ll keep your promise for you."
Ron’s consciousness was already fading, drifting in and out with thoughts left unspoken, until he slipped into slumber.
He saw Tucker again, right there before him.
"Tucker, look... I finally made the Beautiful Voice Perfume. Now we can sing together. But now... I almost don’t want to give it to you."
"Sorry... I can’t sing with you anymore. So... will you sing those awful songs alone for me?"
"Don’t wait for me... but don’t forget me, either."
"Just keep singing those off-key tunes... and remember me always."
